To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the adsorption of large molecules on Immobilines is due to the presence of small amounts of aggregates of Immobilines, that these aggregates have a molecular mass in excess range 1000–2000 Da, and that they are formed during gel filtration on Sephadex G10.
the adsorption of large molecules onto IPGEF gel is not due to small aggregates of Immobilines.
adsorption of large protein molecules onto IPGEF gel is caused by the presence of a minor component of the Immobilines, which is present in the IPGEF gel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adsorption of 5 large proteins on IPGEF gells made from 6 different Immobiline preparations.
a minor component of one Immobiline preparation that appears to be a dimer of the major component, which may account for the adsorption of large molecules onto IPGEF.
the adsorption of large, basic proteins on IPGEF gell in the pH range from 4 to 9.5.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adsorption of the large proteins onto IPGEF gel is not due to the presence of aggregates of Immobiline, nor to the presence of small aggregates in the proteins themselves.
the oligomeric nature of the Immobilin preparation is responsible for adsorption of the 5 proteins tested in IPGEF gell.
the adsorption of large protein onto IPGEF is caused by a small contaminant with a pI of approximately 9.0 and molecular mass less than 500 Da, which is present in some Immobiline preparations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adsorption of large, basic proteins onto IPGEF gel in the range of pH 4–9 can be explained by the presence of small aggregates in the Immobiline preparations used.
adsorption onto IPGEF gel is a function of the size and charge of the protein and the oligomeric structure of the Immobilin used to make the IPGEF gel.
the adsorption of large, oligomeric proteins onto IPGEF gel is due to the presence in Immobilines of a low‐molecular‐weight impurity, the nature of which is not known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oligomeric states of Immobiline preparations are important for the adsorption of large protein molecules during IPGEF.
the adsorption of the large proteins is not due to the presence of small aggregates of Immobiline in the gel.
the adsorption of large, oligomeric proteins in IPGEF is not caused by aggregates of Immobiline.
